source.title: Irish News, 3 June 1955, p. 1 ("Antrim County Council: Ballygomartin division result"); Belfast News-Letter, 18 May 1955, p. 8 ("Only one contest in the Antrim County Council elections"); Belfast News-Letter, 2 June 1955, p. 4 ("Local government elections: polling will take place to-day")
source.publisher: Irish News (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: votes read from the result report: Kerr 2,161; Simms 1,502; majority 659; 120 spoiled votes; 36 per cent poll

note: Triennial election of Antrim County Council on the 23 county electoral divisions; nominations received on 17 May 1955, withdrawals to 18 May, and polling on Thursday 2 June 1955 (official notice, Belfast News-Letter, 4 May 1955, p. 1; 'POLLING will take place to-day', Belfast News-Letter, 2 June 1955, p. 4). Only Ballygomartin was contested. Party labels were printed only for the two Ballygomartin candidates, both shown as (U.). The only contest in the county. Wilson Cupples had also been nominated but withdrew before the poll.
